claims.text: The target material is cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi.
Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering will improve the mechanical integrity of AlCrFeNiSi relative to melt-based fabrication.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS will produce a finer microstructure.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS will produce a more homogeneous microstructure with less elemental segregation.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS will lower residual stresses.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS will reduce defects such as porosity and cracks.
Conventionally or additively fabricated CoCrFeNiSi typically exhibits compositional segregation during cooling.
Conventionally or additively fabricated CoCrFeNiSi typically has high residual thermal stresses.
Conventionally or additively fabricated CoCrFeNiSi typically contains substantial porosity and cracks.
High-energy mechanical alloying can achieve atomic-level mixing of the elemental powders.
The proposed process will form a refined, homogeneous, equiaxed microstructure.
The proposed process will minimize segregation at grain boundaries.
Rapid, isothermal SPS consolidation minimizes thermal gradients.
Mechanical alloying and rapid SPS limit the time available for elemental segregation.
Isothermal consolidation reduces residual-stress accumulation associated with rapid cooling in melt-based processing.
Mechanically alloyed and SPS-consolidated AlCrFeNiSi will have higher hardness than conventionally melt-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Mechanically alloyed and SPS-consolidated AlCrFeNiSi will have higher fracture toughness than conventionally melt-fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Mechanically alloyed and SPS-consolidated AlCrFeNiSi will have lower residual stress and a more uniform elemental distribution than the melt-fabricated baseline.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field names CoCrFeNiSi, which contains Co and lacks Al, whereas the hypothesis and scope concern cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi. These are different alloy systems.
